learn.hook: In one train journey across India, you could hear ten languages, taste twenty kinds of rotis and see snow, deserts and beaches. Yet we are all Indians!
points: India has 28 states and 8 union territories. New Delhi is the capital of India.
People in India speak many languages. The Constitution lists 22 languages in its Eighth Schedule, including Hindi, Tamil, Bengali, Marathi and Assamese.
India has snowy mountains, hot deserts, green forests, long coasts and wide plains. So people's food, clothes and homes are different in different places.
People of many faiths live together and enjoy one another's festivals.
We celebrate national festivals together: Republic Day (26 January), Independence Day (15 August) and Gandhi Jayanti (2 October).

example.q: People in Ladakh wear thick woollen clothes, while people in Kerala wear light cotton. Think it through: why?
steps: Ladakh is high in the mountains and is very cold.
Kerala is near the sea and is warm and humid.
People choose clothes that suit the weather of their place.
example.answer: Because the weather is different: cold in Ladakh, warm in Kerala.

learn.reallife: Look at a ₹10 note. Its value is written in many Indian languages: a small sign of our unity in diversity.

games.title: Days we celebrate
games.prompt: Arrange these days from January to December

games.title: India facts
items: India has 28 states and 8 union territories.
Everyone in India speaks the same language.
Indians speak many languages; 22 are listed in the Constitution's Eighth Schedule.
New Delhi is the capital of India.
New Delhi is India's capital city.
Independence Day is celebrated on 26 January.
Independence Day is on 15 August. 26 January is Republic Day.
The Ashoka Chakra on our flag has 24 spokes.
The navy-blue wheel in the centre of the flag has 24 spokes.
Our national flag has three colours: saffron, white and green.
Saffron at the top, white in the middle and green at the bottom, with the blue Ashoka Chakra.

quiz.q: How many states does India have?
quiz.explain: India has 28 states. It also has 8 union territories.
quiz.mistake: Adds states and union territories together, or confuses the two

quiz.q: How many union territories does India have?
quiz.explain: India has 8 union territories, such as Delhi, Ladakh and Lakshadweep.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up union territories with states

quiz.q: How many languages are listed in the Eighth Schedule of the Indian Constitution?
quiz.explain: The Eighth Schedule lists 22 languages, from Assamese to Urdu.
quiz.mistake: Confuses it with the number of states

quiz.q: What does 'unity in diversity' mean?
options: Everyone must be exactly the same
Each state is a separate country
We are different in many ways but stay together as one country
quiz.explain: Indians have different languages, food and festivals, but we are united as one nation.
quiz.mistake: Thinks unity means everyone being the same

quiz.q: We celebrate Republic Day on
quiz.explain: Our Constitution came into force on 26 January 1950, so we celebrate Republic Day on that date.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up Republic Day with Independence Day

quiz.q: Who wrote India's national anthem, 'Jana Gana Mana'?
quiz.explain: Rabindranath Tagore wrote 'Jana Gana Mana'. Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay wrote the national song 'Vande Mataram'.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the national anthem with the national song

quiz.q: Why do people in different parts of India eat different foods?
options: Food is the same everywhere in India
People are not allowed to eat other foods
Different crops grow in different climates and soils
quiz.explain: Rice grows well in wet places and wheat in drier places, so local food depends on what grows nearby.
quiz.mistake: Does not link food with climate and crops

quiz.q: What is the capital of India?
quiz.explain: New Delhi is the capital. Mumbai, Kolkata and Chennai are large cities and state capitals.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the biggest city must be the capital

teach.ask: Gappu flies over a map: 'Why does India have so many languages, foods and clothes? Is it still one country?'
teach.praise: Amazing! Different languages, food and festivals, but one country. Unity in diversity!
teach.nudge: What things are different across India? And what keeps us together?

learn.hook: Bihu in Assam, Onam in Kerala, Pongal in Tamil Nadu: every state has its own festivals, dances and tasty food. Let's go on a culture trip!
points: Many festivals are linked to harvests: Pongal in Tamil Nadu, Bihu in Assam, Onam in Kerala and Baisakhi in Punjab.
Each state has its own dances: Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu), Kathakali (Kerala), Bhangra (Punjab), Garba (Gujarat), Ghoomar (Rajasthan) and Odissi (Odisha).
Each region has special food: dhokla from Gujarat, litti chokha from Bihar, dal baati churma from Rajasthan, and makki di roti with sarson da saag from Punjab.
The Hornbill Festival of Nagaland shows the dances, songs and crafts of the state's many tribes.
Every state has a capital. For example, Dispur is the capital of Assam and Jaipur is the capital of Rajasthan.

example.q: Neha's family is going to see the boat races during Onam. Which state will they visit?
steps: Onam is the harvest festival of Kerala.
Snake-boat races are held on Kerala's backwaters around Onam.

learn.reallife: Next time you eat at a wedding or a food fair, try a dish from another state and find out where it comes from!

quiz.q: Bihu is a festival of which state?
quiz.explain: Bihu is celebrated in Assam with music, dance and feasts.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up festivals of different states

quiz.q: Which dance form comes from Tamil Nadu?
quiz.explain: Bharatanatyam is a classical dance from Tamil Nadu.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the dance forms of different states

quiz.q: Garba is a popular dance of
quiz.explain: Garba is danced in circles in Gujarat, especially during Navratri.
quiz.mistake: Does not link Garba with Gujarat

quiz.q: Dhokla is a well-known snack from
quiz.explain: Dhokla is a soft, steamed snack made from gram flour in Gujarat.
quiz.mistake: Guesses a state for a dish without knowing it

quiz.q: Litti chokha is a famous dish of
quiz.explain: Litti chokha, baked wheat balls stuffed with sattu, is loved in Bihar.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up dishes of nearby states

quiz.q: Kathakali, a dance with colourful face paint, belongs to which state?
quiz.explain: Kathakali comes from Kerala. Dancers wear bright make-up and big costumes.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up classical dances from the south

quiz.q: What is the capital of Rajasthan?
quiz.explain: Jaipur, the Pink City, is the capital of Rajasthan. The other options are cities in Rajasthan too, but not the capital.
quiz.mistake: Picks a famous city of the state instead of its capital

quiz.q: Pongal, Bihu, Onam and Baisakhi are all festivals linked to
quiz.explain: These festivals celebrate the harvest of crops and thank nature.
quiz.mistake: Does not see the common link between these festivals

teach.ask: Gappu wears a tiny pagdi: 'Which state has Bihu? Where is Garba danced? Tell me about India's colours!'
teach.praise: What a colourful trip! Bihu in Assam, Garba in Gujarat and so many tasty dishes!
teach.nudge: Can you tell me where Bihu or Garba come from? What else is special about each state?

learn.hook: Fish and peacocks painted in Bihar, stick-figure dancers painted in Maharashtra: Indian art tells stories in many styles!
points: Madhubani paintings come from Bihar. They use bright colours and pictures of fish, birds and nature.
Warli paintings come from Maharashtra. They use white stick figures of people, animals and trees.
Gond paintings come from Madhya Pradesh and are made with lines and dots. Blue pottery is a famous craft of Jaipur in Rajasthan.
Our national symbols unite all Indians: the tiger is our national animal, the peacock our national bird and the lotus our national flower.
The banyan is our national tree and the mango is our national fruit.

example.q: A painting shows white stick figures dancing in a circle on a brown wall. Think it through: which art form is it?
steps: Madhubani uses bright colours and fish and bird designs.
Warli uses simple white stick figures.
So the painting is Warli art.

learn.reallife: Look around at a craft fair or museum: you may spot Madhubani, Warli or blue pottery. Each tells the story of the place where it was made.

quiz.q: Madhubani paintings come from which state?
quiz.explain: Madhubani art comes from the Mithila region of Bihar.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up Madhubani with Warli

quiz.q: Which art uses simple white stick figures?
quiz.explain: Warli artists of Maharashtra draw people and animals with circles, triangles and lines in white.
quiz.mistake: Thinks every folk art uses bright colours

quiz.q: What is India's national animal?
quiz.explain: The tiger is India's national animal. The elephant is our national heritage animal.
quiz.mistake: Confuses the national animal with other well-known animals

quiz.q: What is India's national bird?
quiz.explain: The peacock, with its colourful tail feathers, is India's national bird.
quiz.mistake: Picks a common bird instead

quiz.q: Which is India's national flower?
quiz.explain: The lotus grows in water and is India's national flower.
quiz.mistake: Picks a popular flower used in festivals

quiz.q: Blue pottery is a famous craft of which city?
quiz.explain: Jaipur in Rajasthan is known for its blue pottery with flower and bird designs.
quiz.mistake: Does not link the craft with Rajasthan

quiz.q: Gond art, made with lines and dots, comes from
quiz.explain: Gond paintings are made by Gond artists in Madhya Pradesh.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up folk arts of different states

quiz.q: Which of these is India's national tree?
quiz.explain: The banyan tree, with roots hanging from its branches, is India's national tree.
quiz.mistake: Picks a useful or common tree instead

teach.ask: Gappu holds a paintbrush: 'Which state paints with stick figures? And what are India's national symbols?'
teach.praise: Wonderful! Warli from Maharashtra, Madhubani from Bihar, and the tiger, peacock and lotus for all of India!
teach.nudge: Can you name a painting style and its state? And what are some of our national symbols?
